content.text: {"headline":"Approve R1: compliant staffing push on general. It lifts the disruption-window service level to 72.5% for ₹2,664 but still falls short of the 80% target.","why":"The extra calls come from the 09:00 pre-approved loan email (MKT-2026-551), not a staffing problem. Loan and new-offer enquiries are running well above forecast and service level dropped to 68% at 09:45. No policy-compliant plan reaches 80% for 11:00-15:15, so R1 was chosen as the best compliant option. It takes the window from 66.0% (no action) to 72.5%, with general at 68.1% and payments at 78.2%. Abandons fall from 6.5% to 5.0%, and the rest of the day is predicted at 81.8%. The plan delays general and payments breaks from 12:00 to 13:00 by 45 minutes. It offers overtime to 19 general agents from 14:15 to 15:15 and deflects 20% of new-offer and balance enquiries to chat from 14:45 to 15:15. It also moves 3 cross-skilled agents from payments to general from 15:00 to 16:00.","trade_offs":["P2 (81.9%, ₹225) and P3 (85.3%, ₹3,780) would hit target, but both use a known-issue IVR message. That breaks CX-01 because there is no confirmed outage or incident.","R2 costs ₹144 less (₹2,520) and protects payments slightly better (78.9%), but general drops to 65.4% and the overall window to 71.2%.","P4 costs more (₹4,005) and does worse (69.1%). P1 is free but makes things worse than no action (63.7%).","R1 delays payments breaks and moves 3 agents off payments from 15:00, yet payments still holds at 78.2%, above the 75.9% it would see with no action."],"watch":"General will still sit around 68% during the window, below target. Check overtime uptake from the 19 agents and whether loan-enquiry volume keeps rising. If marketing or IT confirms an issue that allows a compliant IVR message, or if demand worsens, revisit the plan."}
